title: Console compact inspectors & cost census - MVP scope reduction and acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Deliver a minimal, battle-tested console surface that provides high-signal route-level insights (latency, error, token cost) and a compact tracing/inspector flow for operators while deferring lower-value visualizations and advanced slicing (per-token waterfall, full span flamegraphs) to later releases. This ticket captures the scope cuts, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the reduced-surface MVP.
scope_included: Per-route summary card: avg latency p50/p95, request rate, error rate, estimated per-token cost (sampled)
Compact top-5 slow routes list with quick-link to lightweight trace inspector
Lightweight trace inspector: single-span view with sampled input/metadata, timeline scrub, and link to raw logs
Cost census: aggregated cost by model family and route (7-day window), with percent delta vs prior week
Rollout flags: per-org feature flag + canary cohort (5% of orgs)
scope_removed_or_deferred: Full token-level waterfall for long responses (deferred)
Per-user cost attribution and billing exports (deferred to Dedicated billing workstream)
High-cardinality trace sampling UI and span flamegraphs (deferred)
Live streaming trace timeline with real-time updates (deferred)
Route-level anomaly detection & automated alerts (shipped as follow-up)
rationale_and_tradeoffs: Shipping a compact surface reduces frontend implementation time by ~60% and avoids backend index schema changes required for token-level telemetry
Accept reduced fidelity in exchange for earlier org-wide rollout and to get feedback from SRE and early customers
Deferring per-user billing prevents coupling console launch to Dedicated billing contract timing
Risk: some SRE workflows will lack deep timing granularity—mitigation: include one-click link to raw logs and define follow-up sprint to add waterfall for top problematic routes
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Per-route summary cards render for 95% of routes in staging within 4s and match backend query results for latency/cost metrics
AC2: Compact inspector loads sampled trace payloads (max 50KB) under 3s for 95th percentile in staging
AC3: Cost census aggregates model-family costs correctly over 7-day windows and shows delta vs prior week; spot-check against billing CSV shows <= 2% variance
AC4: Feature flag gating works: canary orgs see new console and non-canary orgs see old console until ramp to 100%
AC5: E2E test coverage exists for route card rendering, inspector link flow, and cost census computation (smoke tests pass in CI)
AC6: Documentation: console release notes + short runbook for SRE with instructions to use raw logs link and how to request deeper telemetry
decisions: Decision: Use sampled traces (1 in 1000 by default) for inspector surface to avoid increased storage and index costs
Decision: Cost census will be computed from summarized usage tables (daily aggregates) rather than raw per-request tokens to speed queries
Decision: Defer per-user billing integration to Dedicated billing milestone to avoid scope coupling
Decision: Expose a single 'open raw log' CTA in inspector for any additional debugging needs
qa_and_rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): backend aggregation job runs for 48 hours; validate cost census against billing export; enable inspector for internal orgs
Phase 2 (canary): enable feature flag for 5% orgs; monitor errors, latency, and support tickets for 7 days
Phase 3 (ramp): increment to 25% then 100% if no critical issues; wait 72 hours between increments
Rollback criteria: >2% increase in 95th percentile render latency or >0.5% of sessions hit inspector errors -> immediate rollback to previous console surface
Post-launch: schedule 2-week feedback window with SRE and top 5 early customers to capture missing telemetry needs
